title: Body recorded by another cell: the body-dependent witness data through links

key_results.statement: Two-cell setting with initial state $|\phi\rangle_p\otimes|\beta_0\rangle_b\otimes|\chi\rangle$, $|\chi\rangle=|\chi_1\rangle\otimes|\chi_2\rangle$, $\phi_h\ne0$: $|\Psi(\lambda)\rangle=|\beta_0\rangle_b\otimes\sum_h\phi_h|h\rangle_p\otimes e^{-\mathrm iH_h\lambda}|\chi\rangle$ with $H_h=K_h+B_{\beta_0}+J$, so the body stays at $\beta_0$ for every $\lambda$.

$W^{(\beta_0)}(h,h';\lambda)=\big|\langle\chi|e^{\mathrm i(K_{h'}+B_{\beta_0}+J)\lambda}e^{-\mathrm i(K_h+B_{\beta_0}+J)\lambda}|\chi\rangle\big|^2$ for every $\lambda\ge0$: the single-cell formula (6.6) with $B_{\beta_0}\to B_{\beta_0}+J$ on the medium $c_1c_2$.
For $J=0$ the body-dependent part of the witness data vanishes exactly: $\Delta W^{(\beta_0)}(h,h';\lambda)=0$ for every $\lambda\ge0$.

The body-dependent part of the cubic coefficient vanishes: $\Delta c_3^{(\beta_0)}=\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi|B_{\beta_0}\tilde D^2|\chi\rangle=\langle\chi|[B_{\beta_0},\tilde D^2]|\chi\rangle/(2\mathrm i)=0$, because $B_{\beta_0}$ acts on $c_2$ and $\tilde D^2$ on $c_1$.
Operator form of the body-dependent quartic coefficient: $\Delta c_4^{(\beta_0)}(h,h')=\tfrac16\langle\chi|\{\tilde D,[B_{\beta_0},[J,D]]\}|\chi\rangle$.

For $J=\sum_kP_k\otimes Q_k$ in the product state: $\Delta c_4^{(\beta_0)}(h,h')=-\tfrac23\sum_k\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi_1|P_k\tilde D^2|\chi_1\rangle\,\operatorname{Im}\langle\chi_2|B_{\beta_0}Q_k|\chi_2\rangle$, independent of the decomposition of $J$.

On a chain with the probe recorded by $c_1$ and the body by $c_{r+1}$, the body-dependent part of $D(s)=e^{\mathrm iMs}De^{-\mathrm iMs}$, $M=K_{h'}+B_{\beta_0}+\sum_{k=1}^{L-1}J_k$, is $\delta D(s)=\frac{(\mathrm is)^{r+1}}{(r+1)!}Z_r+O(s^{r+2})$ with $Z_r=[B_{\beta_0},[J_r,[\cdots[J_1,D]\cdots]]]$ and $Z_0=[B_{\beta_0},D]$.

On a chain of cells with nearest-neighbour links, the probe recorded by $c_1$, the body by $c_{r+1}$ ($0\le r\le L-1$) and a product initial state: $\Delta W^{(\beta_0)}(h,h';\lambda)=O(\lambda^{3+r})$ as $\lambda\to0^+$.
In the two-qubit example (8.18), for $i\ne j$: $\Delta\alpha^{(\beta_0)}(h_i,h_j;\lambda)=-\tfrac23\,g\,\beta_0\,|i-j|\,\lambda^3+O(\lambda^4)$.

In the two-qubit example (8.18) with the link $J=g\,\sigma_z\otimes\sigma_z$: $\Delta c_4^{(\beta_0)}(h_i,h_j)=0$, hence $\Delta W^{(\beta_0)}=O(\lambda^5)$ and $\Delta\alpha^{(\beta_0)}=O(\lambda^4)$.

definitions.name: Links between neighbouring cells of a chain
Number of links between the probe's cell and the body's cell on a chain
Quartic coefficient of the witness data expansion
Leading body-dependent operator on a chain

open_issues: For r ≥ 2 only the bound (8.16) is shown; the coefficient of the order 3+r term in λ, and whether it is generically nonzero, are not computed.
For the link J = g σz ⊗ σz, the first nonzero body-dependent order is not determined.
The operator results (8.8), (8.10) and (8.16) do not use the product form of the initial medium state, only (8.11) does; non-product medium states are outside the scope.

consistency_checks.check: With J = 0, (8.10) and (8.11) vanish because [J, D] = 0 and Δc3 = 0 by (8.8), in agreement with the exact statement (8.4); on the chain, without links no word in (8.15) reaches the cell c_{r+1} for r ≥ 1.

With the body operator equal to β0 times the identity, the phase factors cancel in (8.3), so ΔW = 0 for every λ, consistent with the commutator in (8.10) and the factor Im⟨β0 Q_k⟩ in (8.11) vanishing.

Body recorded by c1 (r = 0): the support bound (8.16) allows order λ³, and the coefficient is the term Im⟨B_β0 D̃²⟩ = ⟨[B_β0, D̃²]⟩/(2i) of (6.11), which is also what the general λ³ coefficient Im⟨M D̃²⟩ of Step 3 gives.
